title: StratusBio - Incident postmortem follow-up
summary: Follow-up on the 2025-07-08 production incident where inference latency spiked and some requests timed out. Reviewed root cause (KV cache compaction bug + autoscaler behavior), recent mitigations (rollback to stable model variant, increased cache size, short-term scaling policy), and next steps (patch rollout, extended benchmarking, enhanced alerting and SLO updates). Agreed owners and due dates for action items.
action_items: Maya (Redwood) - finalize KV compaction patch and open PR by 2025-07-14
Ravi (StratusBio) - run the 48-hour load benchmark on dedicated cluster and share results by 2025-07-20
Alex (Redwood) - provide updated canary playbook and rollback steps by 2025-07-13
Nina (StratusBio) - validate autoscaler policy changes in staging by 2025-07-16
Jordan (Redwood CSM) - schedule executive summary + security FAQ for StratusBio by 2025-07-17
next_steps: Share patched runtime build and deployment notes (Maya)
StratusBio runs extended benchmark and shares traces (Ravi)
Joint canary on lower-traffic model route next week
Update SLOs and alert thresholds; add eviction-rate alert for K V cache
Redwood to send SOC 2 / audit-log excerpts relevant to incident on request
header:
Date: 2025-07-10
Start: 15:30 PDT
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM), Dr. Ellen Park (StratusBio CTO), Ravi Kumar (StratusBio SRE), Nina Lopez (StratusBio DevOps), Samir Anand (StratusBio Product)
transcript: 00:00 - Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we wanted to run through the postmortem follow up from Wednesday's outage, um about an hour? 62 minutes today. thanks for making time.
00:11 - Dr. Ellen Park: Thanks Alex. Appreciate Redwood getting this scheduled quickly. We need the timeline and concrete mitigations — execs are asking for a short summary too.

00:20 - Maya Patel: Hi all, quick context: root cause is our investigation shows a bug in the KV cache compaction path under high concurrent writes, combined with autoscaler not triggering strongly enough for the model variant we were using. two things together pushed latency over the SLO and caused downstream timeouts.
00:35 - Ravi Kumar: yeah we saw the K V cache eviction rate spike; evictions were 5x normal. some requests hit a fallback path that wasn't warm so those took like 10s and timed out at the app layer.

00:48 - Nina Lopez: to be clear, we had pinned the route to the newer quantized variant for cost reasons, which had a smaller memory profile and triggers compaction more often. maybe that was a mistake during the traffic bump.
01:05 - Alex Chen: right, so two levers: model variant memory footprint + cache compaction bug. Maya, can you describe the compaction bug in plain terms?

01:18 - Maya Patel: sure. the runtime's compaction periodically defragments K V segments. under churn it would incorrectly calculate segment boundaries leading to a transient drop in available slot accounting — effectively the cache thought it had more free slots than it did, so writes caused evictions and cache thrashing. in extreme cases the eviction loop increased lock contention and added latency. it's subtle, not a hardware issue.
01:45 - Dr. Ellen Park: And that only shows up with high concurrency? we can't reproduce in our staging workload which is lower concurrency.
01:53 - Maya Patel: correct. our replay of production load at peak concurrency reproduced it. small workloads won't trigger the pathological boundary condition.
02:10 - Samir Anand: what about autoscaler — why didn't it spin up more nodes?

02:16 - Alex Chen: good question. our autoscaler policy for dedicated clusters had a cooldown and target metric set to p95 latency, but since eviction spikes are short-lived and p95 didn't cross the threshold early enough, it didn't upscale quickly. we need a better metric—eviction-rate or cache-miss-rate might be a better trigger.
02:35 - Ravi Kumar: we also saw a misconfigured max per-node concurrency in the route config; combined, nodes hit saturation faster.

02:44 - Maya Patel: mitigation steps we took: 1) rolled back to the stable non-quantized model variant for the hot route, 2) temporarily increased cache size on the fleet, 3) adjusted autoscaler to a more aggressive policy while we patch, and 4) added short-term alerting for high eviction-rate.

03:00 - Dr. Ellen Park: the rollback helped — latencies returned to normal within ~8 minutes. thanks for that. question: does the rollback increase cost significantly? execs want a cost estimate for this week.
03:14 - Alex Chen: yes some cost increase — Maya can provide ballpark. but it's limited and temporary until the patch is rolled.
03:20 - Maya Patel: ballpark is about +12-18% on the dedicated pool for the rollback and increased sizing, depending on traffic. we'll send a short supporting sheet.
03:33 - Nina Lopez: can you also share where logs and traces are? we need full request traces for our compliance team.

03:40 - Jordan Lee: absolutely. we'll share the trace dump and a filtered set of audit logs. Redwood retains the necessary audit trails; we'll highlight the entries relevant to the incident. also happy to share SOC 2 control mappings on request.
03:58 - Samir Anand: okay good. next, timeline for permanent fix?

04:03 - Maya Patel: we're on it. dev has a fix for the compaction accounting logic. we need QA plus a safe rollout plan. I expect a PR by Mon (2025-07-14), internal QA the next two days, then a canary on a low-traffic route.
04:20 - Ravi Kumar: we want the canary in our staging with a traffic mirror for a 48-hour run. we'll run our own replay too.
04:27 - Maya Patel: that works. recommended plan: patch in runtime -> canary on non-critical route -> monitor eviction-rate/latency for 48h -> promote if green. rollback steps are the same as before.
04:43 - Dr. Ellen Park: on monitoring, can we add a dedicated alert that triggers before p95 moves? Something like sustained eviction-rate > X for Y minutes.
04:53 - Alex Chen: agreed. we'll propose concrete thresholds after we look at peak metrics. likely eviction-rate > 1000/min sustained for 5m or a sharp per-node lock wait increase.
05:10 - Nina Lopez: also please document the autoscaler tuning we used; we changed the cooldown to 30s and lower threshold. need to replicate in staging once patch lands.
05:20 - Maya Patel: noted. we'll provide the autoscaler diff as part of the canary playbook.
05:28 - Ravi Kumar: a couple of nitty-gritty items — request tracing IDs we saw were missing some spans due to an agent-side sampling setting. could that be Redwood's sampling config?
05:38 - Maya Patel: possible — we had a sampling mismatch on the telemetry side during the spike. we'll audit that and ensure full-sampling for the canary window.
05:48 - Alex Chen: also compliance: Jordan, can you confirm what we can share re: audit logs and KMS usage?

05:55 - Jordan Lee: yes. we can share a redacted set of audit logs and confirm KMS operations. for anything deeper we can open an IDA or support ticket, but initial artifacts we can provide this week.
06:05 - Dr. Ellen Park: perfect. one more question: is this something other customers will hit?

06:12 - Maya Patel: potentially, but only customers with similar high-concurrency workloads and small-model variants. we've flagged the more at-risk customers and pushed a preventative config to a few who asked.
06:25 - Samir Anand: ok, do we need a customer-facing postmortem doc?
06:30 - Alex Chen: yes Jordan will draft a public-facing incident summary (non-sensitive) and we'll circulate it internally to the StratusBio incident stakeholders. Jordan?
06:36 - Jordan Lee: I'll prepare a 1-pager and a technical appendix for your SREs. aim for delivery by 2025-07-17.
06:45 - Ravi Kumar: thanks. about the benchmark — we'll include steady state and burst windows and focus on worst-case tail latencies, plus mem/eviction metrics.
06:55 - Maya Patel: good. for the patch, I want to note a small risk: compaction code touches low-level runtime; we'll add an extra canary gate and safety checks to avoid regressions.
07:05 - Dr. Ellen Park: understood. what about longer-term: do we plan to change model routing defaults to avoid small-memory quantized variants for hot routes?

07:13 - Alex Chen: yes a new routing policy is in discussion: route-by-traffic-profile so hot routes stay on larger-memory variants unless cost overrides explicitly requested. we'll include that in the roadmap.
07:24 - Nina Lopez: Alright. can we get a checklist of what's changing in the next two weeks?
07:30 - Maya Patel: sure. checklist: PR by 7/14, QA 7/15-7/16, staging canary 7/17-7/19, joint benchmark 7/20, promote/monitor 7/21-7/23. I'll file this publicly in the ticket.
07:45 - Samir Anand: that's reasonable. also reach out if the cost delta looks different.

07:50 - Alex Chen: action items recap: Maya patch PR, Alex will send canary + rollback runbook, Jordan will draft customer-facing summary and supply audit logs, Ravi/Nina run benchmarks and validate autoscaler staging. agreed?
08:05 - Ravi Kumar: agreed.
08:08 - Dr. Ellen Park: agreed. thanks everyone. small ask: please include a short exec summary with the root cause and one-line mitigation for leadership.
08:18 - Jordan Lee: will do.
08:22 - Maya Patel: i'll also include timeline artifacts and the metric charts used to detect the issue — we'll attach them to the ticket.
08:30 - Alex Chen: great. any other safety or security concerns?
08:34 - Nina Lopez: none from our side, but we may ask for KMS operation logs if security requests them; Jordan you mentioned those are available?
08:40 - Jordan Lee: yes, we can provide KMS operation logs and key rotation audit lines as needed; may require a support ticket for full export.
08:48 - Dr. Ellen Park: ok that's fine. last thing: can Redwood run a short tabletop on incident response with our on-call folks next week?
08:55 - Alex Chen: yes happy to run a 60-minute tabletop — Jordan will coordinate calendars.
09:03 - Jordan Lee: I'll send invites for a 60-min tabletop and include the canary playbook as pre-read.
09:10 - Alex Chen: thanks all. we'll follow up with the PR link, playbook, and the exec summary. meeting closed.
